title: Belong em Ação — M8: Wellbeing and Service Recovery

scenes.script_line: Second lever: sleep. It is the strongest wellbeing determinant of a stay, almost always compromised by operational causes, not design. Total blackout verified, not assumed. Maintenance noise at an agreed hour. Night-time quiet explained warmly on arrival, not as a house rule. And never knocking on a door before ten in the morning without an express request. People who sleep well forgive almost anything; people who sleep badly forgive nothing — and the reason given in the review is rarely sleep.

scenes.script_line: Third lever: choice. Control over your own time is one of the strongest recovery factors there is — which is why freedom is a value of ours, not a brochure adjective. We do not over-programme, over-explain or interrupt. Fourth: quiet and pace. We are the antidote to the city, with concrete consequences: no rushing a table, no loud music at the pool at three in the afternoon, no vacuuming a corridor at half past eight. In doubt between adding and removing, remove.

scenes.script_line: Before complaints, the list of what must never happen, because it is the source of most of them. A guest in front of a team member who does not acknowledge them. A guest passed between three people for a simple question. A guest waiting without knowing why. A guest hearing two versions of the same answer. A guest sensing the team in conflict or short- staffed. A guest forced to repeat themselves. And worst: a guest who leaves with a complaint we never knew about.

scenes.script_line: The protocol. Four steps, in this order. One: acknowledge. Immediately and without defending. You do not argue with a guest's perception — you deal with it. Two: own it. Whoever hears a complaint owns it until it is resolved, even if the fix belongs to another department. Passing it on is not resolving it; following through is. Three: resolve within the hour — if that is impossible, report back every hour until it is done. Silence turns a problem into an incident. Four: close the loop. One contact before departure, confirming it was resolved. The most forgotten step, and the one weighing most on the final rating.

scenes.script_line: Two notes. First: a problem solved within the hour is a story the guest tells friends; a problem that drags on is a story they tell on a review platform. Speed is not courtesy, it is strategy. Second: you do not buy a guest's forgiveness. Research in hospitality shows a well-recovered failure can generate as much loyalty as faultless service, or more — but also that over-compensation backfires, shifting the gesture from care to transaction. Resolve, acknowledge, offer a proportionate gesture. Not three free nights for a tap.
